subject: Sequenced MAP: escrow for DPA signing window & MSA order-form dependencies
messages:
From: Anna Li <anna.li@biomedcorp.com>
To: jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com
Cc: BiomedCorp Procurement <procurement@biomedcorp.com>
Date: 2028-05-22T09:12:00Z
Subject: Sequenced MAP: escrow for DPA signing window & MSA dependencies

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for the recent demo — the team liked the latency numbers. Procurement asked me to share a few constraints up front so we can stage things in the MAP. Two asks:

1) Our legal team needs a target DPA signing window before MSA finalization — specifically we need confirmation whether a 30-day escrow condition is acceptable as an interim measure while legal finalizes some subprocessor language.
2) We want the mutual action plan to explicitly call out the order-form (billing/pricing) as the final gating item once MSA+DPA are agreed.

I've attached a short procurement_requirements.xlsx with the baseline timelines and our internal reviewers. Can you send a draft MAP with owners, firm target dates, and what would be required to take the order form to signature?

Anna Li
Director, Strategic Procurement
BiomedCorp

Attachment: procurement_requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Anna Li <anna.li@biomedcorp.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com, karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2028-05-22T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Sequenced MAP: escrow for DPA signing window & MSA dependencies

Anna — thanks for the clear constraints and the sheet. Draft MAP attached (MAP_draft_20280522.pdf). High level plan below; I've kept the milestones conservative but included an accelerated path if BiomedCorp can commit to a 2-week security review slot and provide a prioritized list of DPA redlines.

Proposed MAP (milestones & gating):
- Week 0 (today): Intake + procurement requirements received (done)
- Week 1: Security questionnaire review (owner: Laura Bennett, action: provide SOC2 artifact & encryption KMS notes)
- Week 2: Technical pilot window / IP access (owner: Jordan Blake)
- Week 3: Legal redlines consolidated (owner: Karthik Iyer)
- Week 4: MSA markups agreed; DPA initial sign-off window (conditional escrow triggered if DPA redlines remain unresolved)
- Week 5: Order form finalization & pricing confirmation (owner: BiomedCorp procurement)
- Week 6: Signature (MSA + DPA + Order form) or staged signature (MSA+DPA signed; order form countersigned within 14 days)

Escrow and conditional signing note: we can accept an escrow-based interim arrangement where the DPA remains conditionally pending and the escrow commitment (verified provider + funds or transfer mechanism) is documented in the MAP. That allows procurement to proceed with PO routing while legal finishes subprocessor and KMS language. If BiomedCorp prefers not to use escrow, fallback is a hard hold on order-form signature until DPA final.

Action items I propose now:
- BiomedCorp: confirm escrow provider (if acceptable) and the internal reviewer for DPA redlines (name/email).
- Redwood: Laura will send SOC2 evidence and an encryption summary by EOD tomorrow; Karthik will prepare an MSA+DPA redline summary for your counsel.
- Schedule: propose a 30-minute sync this Thursday 8am PT / 11am ET to triage redlines and agree owners.

I've attached the MAP draft that maps this plan into specific owners and dependencies.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

Attachment: MAP_draft_20280522.pdf (MAP with timeline & owners)

From: Michael Soto <michael.soto@biomedcorp.com>
To: jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Anna Li <anna.li@biomedcorp.com>, procurement@biomedcorp.com
Date: 2028-05-25T14:29:00Z
Subject: Re: Sequenced MAP: escrow for DPA signing window & MSA dependencies

Jordan — appreciate the MAP. A couple quick clarifications from legal/procurement after reviewing the draft:

> On 2028-05-22 Jordan Blake wrote:
> > Escrow and conditional signing note: we can accept an escrow-based interim arrangement...

1) For escrow we need the provider to be a recognized custodian (e.g., IronClad Escrow or a bank escrow). We also need the trigger conditions clearly defined: what constitutes "resolution" of DPA redlines so funds/keys are released.
2) Our legal flagged subprocessor cascading obligations in Section 6 of the DPA. Do you have a firm stance on whether Redwood imposes flow-down obligations to downstream subprocessors, and how KMS access is audited?

I've attached Biomed_DPA_redlines.docx with inline comments. If we can get a marked MSA+DPA back with comment responses by next Tuesday (2028-05-30), we can meet your Week 6 target assuming security sign-off. Otherwise procurement will need a signed conditional order form that references the escrow arrangement.

Thanks,
Michael Soto
Sr. Manager, Procurement Operations
BiomedCorp

Attachment: Biomed_DPA_redlines.docx (docx with inline comments)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Michael Soto <michael.soto@biomedcorp.com>, Anna Li <anna.li@biomedcorp.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com, laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2028-05-30T16:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Sequenced MAP: escrow for DPA signing window & MSA dependencies

Michael / Anna — thanks for the redlines and the timeline. Quick responses inline and an updated play for accelerating to signature: 

1) Escrow provider + trigger: We can accept a named third-party escrow (Redwood has used ThirdBridge Escrow for prior customers). Trigger for release = mutual written confirmation that DPA redlines affecting data residency/subprocessor risk have been resolved or an agreed remediation plan is in place with firm deadlines (both parties sign off). We'll document the exact release conditions in a short escrow addendum attached to the MAP.

2) Subprocessors & KMS: Redwood requires flow-down obligations to subprocessors for data processing activities that materially affect customer data. For KMS, we do not share raw keys: we provide customer-keyed envelope encryption with audit logs for key access. Laura will attach the KMS summary and audit cadence this week.

Accelerated plan (conditional):
- Tue 2028-05-30: Redwood returns MSA+DPA with point-by-point responses to the Biomed redlines (owner: Karthik Iyer).
- Wed–Thu 2028-05-31 to 2028-06-01: Biomed legal reviews and flags any remaining high-priority items.
- Fri 2028-06-02: Mutual confirmation of DPA language or agreement to escrow addendum.
- Mon 2028-06-05: Order form prepared for signature (procurement owner: BiomedCorp).
- Tue 2028-06-06: Target signature (MSA + DPA signed or MSA+DPA + escrow addendum signed; order form countersigned within 7 business days).

If Biomed cannot commit to the review window above, we will proceed with the conditional order form (references escrow addendum) to avoid blocking procurement lead times.

Action owners & next steps: 
- BiomedCorp: confirm escrow provider and internal legal reviewer by EOD 2028-05-31.
- Redwood: Karthik will send the marked MSA+DPA by EOD 2028-05-30; Laura will provide SOC2 + KMS audit summary by 2028-05-31.
- All: book a 30-minute redlines triage on 2028-05-31 9am PT if that works for your team.

Thanks — we'll get the marked docs over and annotate change rationale for any DPA flow-downs. If procurement wants an explicit checklist we can include a short sign-off table in the MAP so routing queues at Biomed procurement are clear.

— Jordan Blake
